decision: What matters to people struggling to replace or adapt an unsatisfactory mattress, and which unresolved mechanism merits the next real test?
grain: 8 bounded illustrative account histories (one licensed workshop participant + seven separate public authors); neither identity independence nor respondent representativeness established

episodes.desired_progress: Wake restored for work and family
episodes.reported_outcome: Purchase reported; older mattress still used/retained; achieved rest unknown

episodes.tipping_context: Sleep discomfort and heat sensitivities prompted material experimentation
episodes.path_x: Changed foam/latex layers for approximately two months, keeping dated notes and requesting samples
episodes.desired_progress: Comfortable, cooler support for two sleepers
episodes.reported_outcome: Reported a few nights on latest configuration; durability not established

episodes.tipping_context: Pair sought supportive comfort while avoiding full replacement expense
episodes.path_x: Reported testing multiple components together, settling on layered DIY bed and planning to replace one worn component
episodes.desired_progress: Maintain support, comfort and controllable maintenance cost
episodes.reported_outcome: Reports three years of comfort, base wear and anticipated component replacement; not independent objective verification

episodes.path_x: Replaced and rearranged latex elements repeatedly

episodes.tipping_context: Difficult return recovery after many mattress trials
episodes.path_x: Reported refund after failed courier/donation, reused foam, planned DIY switch

mechanisms.title: Perceived ability to recover from a failed mattress purchase conditions action
mechanisms.claim: When failure feels hard to reverse, buyers may delay, redirect or abandon a mattress purchase even while discomfort persists.
mechanisms.rival: Retailer reputation, price, product differences, and readiness may matter more than return logistics.

case_assessments.reason: A contemplated Groupon purchase was abandoned partly over what would happen if it failed; Costco differs in seller, product and shopping context.
Sample packs would reportedly have reduced material returns, but this concerns component experiments rather than a new mattress purchase.
The author sold unused parts and planned selective replacement, leaving initial failure-recovery anxiety unspecified.
Recurrent latex softening is alleged but buying/return decisions are not described in enough detail.
A reportedly easy completed return is a contrast to difficult recovery, not evidence of what prompted original purchase.
Reported donation/courier failures followed a return; dozens of alternative causes remain, but removal frictions were tangible.
A missed 120-day trial cutoff is a case of time-bounded recoverability; actual final retailer decision is unknown.
A completed latex refund is reported, yet seller trust and product mismatch are confounded with convenience.

mechanisms.falsifier: Comparable active shoppers demonstrate no difference in real purchase attempts under genuinely different, otherwise-identical pickup/refund conditions.
mechanisms.minimal_test: Randomize verified pickup/refund guarantee within one retailer and mattress, separately measuring paid attempts and completed returns.

mechanisms.title: Short contact and perceived comfort are imperfect proxies for overnight fit
mechanisms.claim: A brief sample or initial comfort judgment can fail to predict sustained comfort, motivating actual-use trials.
mechanisms.rival: Pain may depend on stress, pillow configuration, activities or other health factors rather than the mattress.

case_assessments.reason: The spouse felt a sample and a purchase followed, but no observed overnight result of the new bed appears in this interview.
Builder explicitly reported showroom lying was unlike overnight latex sleeping and iterated layers for comfort.
Month of component experimentation could reflect poor predictiveness of brief feel, but no explicit before/after sampling comparison.
Subjective support reportedly changed over months, not a direct test of momentary showroom feel.
A six-week experience revealed softness dissatisfaction, but no brief-sample expectation is documented.
Many returns alone do not tell whether in-store or short trials predicted overnight comfort.
A temporary period of improved sleep followed by worse nights undermines a one-time comfort reading, though lifestyle was different.
Person reported bed was comfortable to lie on yet caused recurring morning stiffness; work/travel differences may explain some of it.

mechanisms.falsifier: Prospective participants' brief evaluations reliably predict their repeated overnight comfort after adjusting for daily circumstances.
mechanisms.minimal_test: Compare showroom/sample judgments with repeated overnight diaries and actual returns, recording confounding factors.

mechanisms.title: Selective component adjustment can sometimes extend usable comfort
mechanisms.claim: For some users, tuning or replacing a component may sustain progress without replacing an entire mattress.
mechanisms.rival: Extra experimentation, moving components, new-material novelty and high knowledge/time costs could make DIY less effective or economical.

case_assessments.reason: No component modification of the new purchased mattress reported; original bed adjustments belong to Path Y.
The latest DIY build required many layer swaps; outcome only a few nights and total costs not audited.
An assembled layered mattress reportedly worked over three years; replacing the worn base was planned, not verified completed.
Despite long-term experiments and layer changes, author reports the same softening problem—a direct negative case for easy improvement.
A more expensive adjustable air replacement reportedly worked better, but this is an entire bed replacement not low-cost modular repair.
Author repurposed a returned bed and planned DIY components; ongoing sleep success remains unreported.
No adjustable components or repair alternative in reported episode.
Multiple toppers failed; person moved to a local customized complete mattress, not sustained DIY maintenance.

mechanisms.falsifier: Verified repeated trials demonstrate no improvement in retained sleep outcomes or life-cycle cost versus otherwise matched conventional replacement.
mechanisms.minimal_test: Prospectively track component changes, total costs, comfort and retention among consenting DIY and conventional buyers over repeated intervals.

mechanisms.title: Purchase and first impressions do not establish durable Point B
mechanisms.claim: The consumer's desired restorative sleep must be assessed after actual use; buying or briefly liking a mattress does not alone establish success.
mechanisms.rival: An uncomfortable period may be temporary or due to external context, not persistent product failure.

case_assessments.reason: A Costco purchase occurred, but old mattress use and unresolved sleep concern prevented attributing end-state progress.
Only a few nights' improvement reported; no longer-term outcome to determine whether the configuration solved the job.
Reported three-year comfort is an explicitly favorable outcome, in contrast to failure accounts, but no independent verification.
Long histories of replacing materials coexist with reported unsolved perceived support.
First bed was refunded after discomfort, later expensive air bed was reportedly better, showing outcomes differ between purchases.
Repeated completed purchases were followed by failed comfort or recovery, not sustained solved progress.
Writer reports high-cost purchase and intermittent relief, then return to discomfort after trial expiry.
An apparently comfortable initial bed led to refund; outcome of new custom bed was not yet observed.

mechanisms.falsifier: Longitudinal measures of retained use and waking function consistently converge with purchase alone, including initially dissatisfied participants.
mechanisms.minimal_test: Track actual use, attempted modifications, refunds and repeated waking function after purchase rather than using checkout as success.

counterfactuals.scenario: A guaranteed no-cost mattress pickup if the trial fails

human_challenges.finding: A later buyer reports an easy real pickup/refund; that does not reveal whether the pickup guarantee caused purchase.
Another buyer reports failed courier visits and a leftover mattress after refund, challenging universal frictionless recovery.
Another buyer reports missing a trial cutoff, emphasizing that a stated promise is bounded by time and conditions.

counterfactuals.scenario: A physical sample available to a household before purchase

human_challenges.finding: Spouse reportedly touched foam before purchase, but there is no isolation of its effect from seller or timing.
DIY builder reports sample packs would have reduced material returns, but this is a different decision and intervention.
One buyer reports comfort on lying down despite repeated morning stiffness, limiting short-contact inference.

validation_design.predeclared_question: How likely are you to buy this mattress under the exact offer?
validation_design.required_next_test: Prespecify identical scenarios and questions, independent recruited human responses (intent), and separate observed purchasing outcomes for behavioral claims.

warnings: Author-constructed generated responses are not independent respondent samples.
The two SSR means are not intervention effects, market probabilities or rankings.
Reported countercases are qualitative plausibility challenges, not matched human validation.
The original interview has not received human evidence/coding approval.

lead_user_scout.decision: Is adaptive, repairable mattress comfort a meaningful emerging need beyond conventional mattress return guarantees?

trend_candidates.statement: Increasing acceptability of mattress purchasing online
trend_candidates.relevance: Shows evaluation/return may shift away from store, not a proven modular repair trend.
trend_candidates.caveats: Different surveys, years, regions and survey questions; not causal.

trend_candidates.statement: Households may increasingly assemble and replace their own comfort layers
trend_candidates.relevance: First-person examples are discovery seeds, not population adoption or trend direction.
trend_candidates.caveats: Public DIY enthusiasts are highly selected; no longitudinal representative demand data.

candidates.reason: Detailed iterations and notes show advanced activity, but no independently supported important trend or quantified expected benefit.
Three-year repairable arrangement reportedly worked, but intended base replacement is not actual verified cost savings.
Repeated support changes signal burden; material degradation and benefit of an alternative remain unverified.
Many purchases and disposal workarounds alone do not establish advancement ahead of an important trend.

contradictions: R02 reports long-term benefit from modular elements; R03 reports repeated deterioration after latex changes.
R01 reports many trials but only a few nights with a recent configuration, so durability remains unknown.
R07 chose a local custom manufacturer instead of DIY, suggesting advanced DIY practice may not transfer to ordinary shoppers.
lead_user_scout.pyramiding_status: NOT_STARTED; source links are discovery seeds, not referrals or interviews

transfer_hypotheses.statement: Some buyers might benefit from changing support locally after purchase rather than reversing the entire purchase.
transfer_hypotheses.limit: No qualified LU episode and no comparative effect; this is an exploratory research question, not an imported context-return finding.

integrated_research_decision.observed_original: CD01 establishes a historical purchase attempt, not successful Point B.
integrated_research_decision.contrastive_real_accounts: The independently authored posts describe return fulfillment, expired trials, adjustable/replaced components and later discomfort; all are unverified self-reports.
integrated_research_decision.working_interpretation: A promising research axis is managing uncertainty over time: reversibility of the whole purchase versus adjustability/repairability after purchase.
integrated_research_decision.rival_interpretation: The decisive variable might instead be mattress quality/comfort, seller reputation or each sleeper's non-product circumstances.
integrated_research_decision.next_decision: Run separate real tests: initial purchase reversal (same seller/product), longitudinal fit/repair, and sleep-outcome follow-up; do not use SSR to select a winner.
